task.description: WF-03 Step 2 (fix design) for ISS-0427: design a test-only template-clone mechanism to replace per-schema migration replay in test/support/tenant_fixture.ex, precisely specifying the clone mechanism, foreign-key and sequence re-creation, an asserted (not assumed) catalog-level parity check TEST-DESIGNER can turn into a real test, fallback/failure behaviour, and an honest speedup estimate. Test-only scope; production provision_tenant_schema/1 and replay_migrations/2 must not change.

result.summary:
Design written to lib/letflow/design/iss0427-tenant-test-schema-template-clone.md. New test-only module Letflow.Test.TenantTemplate (test/support/tenant_template.ex) with ensure_template!/0, template_schema_name/0, clone_tenant_schema!/1, template_ready?/0, and assert_clone_parity!/2.

MECHANISM (design section 2-4): a fixed-name schema "tenant_template" is built once per BEAM VM/partition database (scripts/test_parallel.sh runs each MIX_TEST_PARTITION in its own database, so 'once' is correctly scoped per-database, not per-suite) via CREATE SCHEMA + the real Ecto.Migrator.run/4 call against tenant_scoped_migrations/0 -- NOT via provision_tenant_schema/1 or replay_migrations/2 themselves (neither fits: no Registration row is ever created for the template, and it must never be reachable via tenant_id_for_schema_name/1 -- verified by inspection that "tenant_template" fails that function's regex today, zero code change needed). TenantFixture.provisioned_tenant!/1 gains an opts[:template] key (:clone default, :replay explicit escape hatch preserving today's exact behaviour) and branches to ensure_template!/0 + clone_tenant_schema!/1 instead of provision_tenant_schema/1 + replay_migrations/1. Existing assert_schema_complete!/2 call is unchanged and still runs as a second, independent layer.

CLONE MECHANISM, per table: CREATE TABLE (LIKE template.<t> INCLUDING ALL), then (a) FK re-add from pg_constraint (contype='f') via pg_get_constraintdef(oid) with the template schema's qualifier textually substituted for the clone's -- this substitution is NOT optional, verified by my own psql probe that pg_get_constraintdef on a re-added FK still names the TEMPLATE's tables unless rewritten, which would silently create live cross-schema FK coupling, an even worse defect than the current FK-less clone; (b) sequence recreation via pg_get_serial_sequence(schema.table, column) (verified the more robust primitive -- a pg_depend deptype='a' walk, which ISSUE-FIXER's diagnosis suggested, returned ZERO rows in my own probe despite ALTER SEQUENCE...OWNED BY having been issued, so I deviated from that suggestion and recorded it as a MINOR conflict per core-directives.md); (c) event_type_registry row copy (template->clone, data only, since replay_migrations/2's 13-row platform-event-type seed is table data LIKE never touches) and (d) schema_migrations row copy so assert_schema_complete!/2's existing versions_missing check reads correctly against a clone.

EVERY CLAIM ABOVE IS PSQL-VERIFIED THIS SESSION, not inherited from the diagnosis unchecked: built throwaway probe_tpl/probe_clone schemas in letflow_dev modelling the real FK+owned-sequence-default shape, confirmed (1) LIKE INCLUDING ALL omits FKs (0 vs 1 in the probe, matching ISSUE-FIXER's 0/22 on the real schema), (2) the FK-qualifier bug above, (3) LIKE INCLUDING ALL RENAMES INDEXES to Postgres's auto-generated default names (events_parent_idx -> events_parent_id_idx, a partial unique index events_partial_idx -> events_parent_id_idx1) -- a NEW finding this design pass added, meaning the parity check must compare index/constraint definitions structurally, never by name, or it will false-fail or worse false-pass; (4) after applying the FK-substitution + sequence-recreation fix, a clone's insert advances ONLY its own sequence (template's last_value provably unaffected) and an FK-violating insert into the clone is correctly rejected. All probe schemas dropped before this handoff was written; git status --porcelain shows only the new design file.

PARITY CHECK (design section 3, the crux per the dispatch): assert_clone_parity!(reference_schema, candidate_schema), catalog-level, symmetric, structural (schema-qualifier-normalized string comparison, never name-based per the index-rename finding). Eight enumerated dimensions: table set, columns (type/nullable/default/collation), constraint kinds+defs as a per-table multiset, indexes as a per-table multiset of normalized indexdef (this single check covers unique/partial/expression indexes for free -- no separate handling needed), sequence-backed-column agreement plus an explicit assertion the candidate's sequence lives IN the candidate schema (the direct mechanical test for the sequence trap), NOT NULL/identity (folded into columns, plus an explicit pg_attribute.attidentity check even though no identity column exists today, so a future one is caught), event_type_registry + schema_migrations row-count/version-set equality (data, not structure), and triggers/comments/collations/privileges each explicitly checked-or-ruled-out with a stated reason (triggers: zero today, documented Postgres exception to INCLUDING ALL, flagged as Open Question OQ-2 for when one is added; comments: zero today, checked anyway; collations: folded into column check; privileges: N/A because this codebase enforces tenant isolation at the app layer via :prefix, not Postgres GRANT/REVOKE -- single shared DB role for all schemas). Two concrete runnable use sites specified for TEST-DESIGNER: (1) template self-check at build time against a genuine replay_migrations/2-built reference schema, so a broken template fails loudly before serving any clone; (2) a permanent test/support/tenant_template_test.exs regression test comparing a real clone against the template on every suite run, all 8 dimensions.

FALLBACK (design section 5): NO silent fallback to replay, by deliberate choice -- a build or clone failure raises (same report_and_raise!-shaped convention TenantFixture already uses), matching the dispatch's own reasoning that silent fallback would hide breakage. Per-test opt-out (opts[:template] = :replay) is the only sanctioned escape hatch and is explicit, never automatic. Staleness (issue-fixer's 'template missing new migrations' risk) is closed structurally, not just checked: each partition's BEAM VM builds its own template fresh at run start, so there is no persistent template artifact that can outlive one run's database lifetime; the build-time self-check (versions in schema_migrations vs tenant_scoped_migrations/0) is what catches a broken build immediately if one occurs.

SCOPE (design sections 1 and 7): zero diff to lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning.ex's provision_tenant_schema/1 or replay_migrations/2 function bodies, zero diff to lib/letflow/sandbox_pool.ex (section 6: confirmed complementary -- SandboxPool already builds pooled schemas via the same raw Ecto.Migrator.run/4 primitive this design's template build uses, so it COULD adopt clone_tenant_schema!/1 later for its own speedup, but that is explicitly optional future work, not designed here, flagged as OQ-4). ISS-0423's Sandbox.mode(:auto)/async scope is explicitly NOT absorbed (section 4.2 states plainly this design does not fix that global-mode defeat of async, and states why no NEW concurrency hazard is introduced regardless). One genuine brush against lib/: the 13-row platform-event-type seed list (@platform_event_type_seed_attrs) is currently PRIVATE to tenant_provisioning.ex, and the template build needs it -- flagged explicitly as Open Question OQ-1 with two named, undecided options (expose a minimal public seeding function vs. build the template via a throwaway real Tenant/Registration + the unmodified replay_migrations/2, discarding the rows after) rather than silently picking one, since option (a) would be the one place this design touches lib/ and that must be an explicit ELIXIR-DEV/REVIEWER decision, not a default silently taken here.

SPEEDUP CLAIM (design section 10), stated honestly per the dispatch's explicit instruction: known -- 2.5x on this host for the BARE clone step alone (354.2ms vs 877.21ms, this session's own re-measured, compile-isolated numbers, NOT the filed 4.9x/2259ms which did not reproduce), expected to hold approximately once FK-readd+sequence-fix+data-copy overhead (small: 22 FK statements, 1 sequence, two small data copies on the real schema) is added, but that FULL-mechanism number is NOT separately measured by this design -- left to TEST-RUNNER/RELEASE-VALIDATOR post-implementation. NOT known and NOT promised: any CI number (ISS-0432's own caveat: ~92% of this host's round-trip cost is Docker Desktop overhead that will not transfer; extrapolated co-located replay cost is roughly 70-100ms, which could shrink the clone path's absolute CI savings to low tens of milliseconds per provisioning even if the ratio direction holds) and any specific total-suite-wall-clock percentage (the filed 755-provisioning count is itself unconfirmed per ISSUE-FIXER's own issue note -- this design does not restate it as fact, and points TEST-RUNNER's Step 4 regression run as the natural place to get a real fresh count and a real fresh before/after).

Invariants (design section 8) and four open questions (section 9, OQ-1 through OQ-4) stated explicitly rather than silently resolved, including OQ-1 above (the one point requiring an ELIXIR-DEV/REVIEWER decision before implementation) and OQ-2 (triggers, forward-looking, not currently applicable). Acceptance-criteria mapping table (design section 11) ties every element of the issue's own stated requirements, plus the sequence/DEFAULT hazard ISSUE-FIXER found that the issue's original text did not mention, to a concrete design section -- no TBD.

No implementation code in the design file -- verified by inspection: the document contains prose, @spec-style type/function signature blocks (bare ```; no elixir fences with function bodies), and one markdown table. No .ex/.exs file under lib/ or test/ was modified by this step.

issues.description: Deviated from ISSUE-FIXER's diagnosis suggestion of using pg_depend (deptype='a') to enumerate sequence-owned columns for recreation. My own psql probe found that query returns ZERO rows for a sequence with a confirmed ALTER SEQUENCE ... OWNED BY relationship on this Postgres version/setup, so it is not a reliable primitive here. Used pg_get_serial_sequence(schema.table, column) instead, verified directly to work correctly. Recorded per core-directives.md's 'Never resolve a conflict silently' -- ELIXIR-DEV should use pg_get_serial_sequence per the design, not pg_depend, and REVIEWER should note this diverges from the diagnosis's exact wording (not from its underlying requirement, which is fully met).

Open Question OQ-1 (design section 9) is a real, undecided fork that determines whether this change's diff surface stays entirely within test/support/ (option b) or makes one small, explicit addition to lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning.ex's public surface (option a, exposing the currently-private platform-event-type seed list/logic). This must be decided before ELIXIR-DEV implements -- flagging now rather than letting ELIXIR-DEV pick silently, since it changes what SECURITY-REVIEWER's gate needs to look at (section 7 currently states 'zero lib/ diff' as true only if option (b) is chosen).
